Only a few years ago, even the simplest image processing operations strained state-of-the-art computers to their limits. 128 x 128 arrays took a lot of memory, and even the most trivial operations required enormous amounts of time. Then, with faster computers and cheaper memory, the technology finally began to catch up. Today, image operations are still time consuming, but it is no longer unthinkable to process 512 x 512 images. Now, imaging sensors are becoming an increasingly important part of closed-loop controllers in robotics, missile guidance, the automatic tracking of moving objects, and other intelligent systems. However, these applications require real-time processing of image sequences, and once again, the demands of image processing are pushing the available technology to its limits.

Interconnection networks are a natural result of advances in computer technology that brought about demands for improved system performance. As computer systems evolved from the batch-processing models of the 1960's to the time-sharing models of the 1970's, their evolution was basically confined within the von Neumann architectural model, with hardware costs being a significant limiting factor. However, contemporary IC technology is creating an entirely new atmosphere; it is now economically feasible to construct a multiple-processor computer system by interconnecting a large number of off-the-shelf processor and memory modules. In addition, because of today's increased performance requirements, the number of functional modules (homogeneous or heterogeneous) in the multiple-processor system normally keeps rising as the domain of applications grows. Trying to counter this trend presents quite a challenge to computer architects.

The World Aerobatic Championships attract some of the most highly skilled aircraft pilots in the world. Coming from four continents, 50 pilots plus crew members met in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, for the 10th championships in August of 1980.

Hewlett-Packard's Model 64005S emulation terminal system lets mainframe users augment existing microprocessor product development tools for their computers with the real-tine, transparent emulation of the HP 64000 logic development system. With RS-232C (V. 24) or current loop interfaces for serial data links to the computer, the HP 64100A development station can be used as an ASCII terminal or as a stand-alone emulation station. Logic analysis is optionally available.

International Memories, Inc., has integrated a single-board controller into its 10M-byte and 20M-byte drives. With the embedded controller, IMI's 7710/7720 drives achieve a 35-ms average access time with a 75-watt power requirement.

The world's largest producer of Oriental rugs is, surprisingly, Holland. One of the Leading producers of made-in-Holland Oriental rugs, Van Heugten BV (a subsidiary of Heuga Holding) is using a computerized rug design and manufacturing system offering color graphic displays and ink-jet spray technology.

Step Engineering's latest addition to their line of firmware integration and test stations is the CCI, RS232-based system. A target processor's programs can be automatically loaded and its operaton can be monitored and controlled over the CCI's serial links. CCI is a universal peripheral giving other systems bit-slice capability for development or test purposes.

Datel-Intersil's APP-48 is a 48-column, panel-mount thermal printer with built-in control and interface electronics. Measuring 8.12" × 2.84" × 8.32" and weighing less than six pounds, the unit fits into control panels or inside larger OEM products.

Remote sensing by satellite is one of the more dramatic technological advances made possible in part by the computer. NASA's Landsat satellite, one of many remote sensing systems, is currently being used by a number of countries to evaluate their natural resources. Most of the information gathered by the sensors would be lost without computers fast enough to process the enormous quantities of transmitted data.

CNR has developed a series of high-speed programmable array processors, designated Mars-232, tailored for use in systems with demanding throughput requirements. In the basic configuration, Mars can perform the industry-standard 1K complex fast Fourier transform in 1.05 ms. The more comprehensive multiprocessor configurations achieve higher performance levels.

Honeywell has added four DPS-8 large-scale host computers to its Control Program 6 multiuser systems as part of a program to expand the growth path for current users of the CP-V and CP-6 operating systems. Accommodating up to 120 simultaneous users, the models added are the DPS 8/62C, the DPS 8/44C in single- and dual-processor configurations, and DPS 8/20C.

An excellent and well-rounded anthology, the second edition of Introduction to Computer Architecture presents both the theoretical and the practical aspects of computer architecture. The book's focus makes it ideal either for persons wanting an overview of what goes into a computer or for those who actually want to build one.

On first sight, the title of this anthology is quite misleading. Not one of the numerous "how to write a better program" books, On the Construction of Programs is, instead, a collection of papers presented at a seminar at Queen's University (Belfast) in 1979. The central theme trying them together is a discussion of parallel processing and other issues at the fore-front of language design.

Despite the fact that we are already up to our eyebrows in texts on microcomputers, Microcomputer Interfacing by G. J. Lipovski is a valuable addition to the library of both students and practicing engineers. An introduction to the principles and techniques of general microcomputer design that focuses on interfacing problems, the book is a reliable source for novices who need useful information on microcomputer techniques.

Researchers at Battelle Memorial Institute in Columbus, Ohio, are engaged in a six-month international study that is examining the future of plastic credit cards with built-in microprocessors and memories. The study is being sponsored by a number of banks, telephone companies, oil companies, and high-technology manufacturers.

An experimental IBM computer circuit, with switching speeds faster than emitter-coupled logic, but with the low power level and small cell size of transistor-transistor logic, was announced February 25 at Compcon Spring. The circuit was invented by IBM engineers Richard R. Konian and James. L. Walsh, at IBM's East Fishkill, N.Y., facility.

The theory of recursively solvable decision problems, the theory of recursively unsolvable decision problems, the theory of decidable theories, and the theory of undecidable theories are basic to modern logic. The theories of unsolvable problems and undecidable theories establish formal frameworks for questions that cannot, in principle, be resolved by computational means as we understand them. They are analogous to the simpler. impossibility problems involving more restricted means of construction, which the ancients bequeathed to us: the so-called duplication of the cube, the squaring of the circle, or the trisecting of an arbitrary angle by Euclidean ruler and compasses alone, for example. Indeed, recursively unsolvable problems–products of a dogged determination to understand the nature of computation–are analogous to the simpler problem of the impossibility of solving arbitrary polynomial equations by rational operations and radicals, that is, by allowing expanded computational means.

Recent books on microprocessors and their applications have been more like catalogs than textbooks. C. A. Ogdin's Microcomputer Management and Programming, however, is in neither of these categories, although it leans toward the former. This book is meant to educate software professionals and managers who are conversant with software problems about microcomputer hardware. It partially fulfills this intention.

Hughes Aircraft Company is developing a fiber optics communications system for the US Army that will enable a safely concealed gunner to remotely direct a guided missile to a battlefield target. Hughes and its principal subcontractor, ITT Electro-Optical Products Division, are working on techniques to enable communication between an airborne missile and a gunner at the launch site via a fine fiber-optic thread. Program officials say the system has the potential to provide the basis for a lowcost lock-on-after-launch anti-armor missile with extended range and immunity to enemy countermeasures.

Five years ago, Arkansas Enterprises for the Blind, in Little Rock, started offering a computer programming course on an individual, informal basis; today, the course is part of its regular curriculum.

A new system for production testing of complex large-scale integrated circuits has been developed by a team of Bell-Northern Research engineers. Now in use at Northern Telecom's semiconductor manufacturing facility in Ottawa, the system is faster and more accurate than any other, approaching the limits of the laws of physics in its operation.

Hewlett-Packard's on-line performance tool, OPT/3000, is an interactive performance measurement package providing software and training that enables users to determine the current workload, memory usage, CPU activity, and I/O traffic of their HP 3000 systems. Based on this information, users can tune individual applications, balance the CPU workload, optimize system performance, and plan future capacity, according to the company.

Josephson technology "shows potential for a generation of computers with major improvements in performance, overall system cost, power requirements, and size," according to a study by M. J. Marcus of IBM's Thomas J. Watson Research Center.*
Advant's Model 1400 portable EPROM programmer uses satellite devices for programming all standard, commercially available PROM families.

To assure that the quality of treated effluent being dumped into South San Francisco Bay by surrounding communities remains consistent with the Clean Water Act and Environmental Protection Agency standards, a complex network of minicomputers and electronic sensors has been developed to continually monitor the sewage as it moves through pipelines and processing plants on its way to the bay.

In the early sixties a tentative proposal was advanced to form a national data bank by linking together some six hundred separate federal repositories of personal data. The proposal envisioned a statistical data bank to beused primarily for research. That many of us were uneasy, to say the least, in the face of such a suggestion was amply demonstrated in the course of subsequent congressional committee hearings; hearings that resulted in the proposal never being formally offered. A decade later many of the objections raised in these hearings were to be vividly underscored by the revelations of the Watergate investigations. Personal data banks can be abused and diverted to purposes far from the original intentions of lawmakers and system designers.

In a move to automate dispatching and billing operations, London-Wide Radio Taxi is adding a Honeywell DPS 6/74 computer system to its West London control center.
